portInfo.description: The Vieux Bassin concentrates the town’s painted maritime image, but a good visit also reaches Sainte-Catherine’s timber church, the Lieutenance and museums associated with Eugène Boudin and Erik Satie. The estuary and Normandy setting are important context. Paris, the D-Day beaches and Mont-Saint-Michel are separate long road decisions, not spare-hour extras after lunch.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Vieux Bassin and Lieutenance, Vieux Bassin/Quai Sainte-Catherine, Lieutenance end, Honfleur: A precise harbour-side start combining maritime views and the historic gateway. Allow about 75 minutes (editorial estimate). Harbour edges are public sightseeing space, not an ocean-cruise landing.

Sainte-Catherine Church, Place Sainte-Catherine, Honfleur: A timber church with a distinct architectural story beyond the harbour photograph. Allow about 45 minutes (editorial estimate). Respect worship and current visitor access.

Eugène Boudin Museum, Rue de l’Homme de Bois, Honfleur: A focused art-history option tied to the town’s painterly identity. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Confirm interior opening/ticket terms; no live fees quoted.

Maisons Satie, Boulevard Charles V, Honfleur: A named museum devoted to Erik Satie with a different theme from painting. Allow about 75 minutes (editorial estimate). Opening and individual accessible-route suitability need checking.

Jardin des Personnalités, Jardin des Personnalités, Seine-front beyond Naturospace, Honfleur: A specific estuary-side garden for a flat outdoor alternative. Allow about 60 minutes (editorial estimate). Wind/rain may favour a shorter route.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Photograph the day’sQSH1/QSH3 pickup information before leaving. The pretty Vieux Bassin is a sightseeing meeting area, not evidence that your ship boards there.

gettingThere.distanceToCity: The official green walking route is 1.6 km, about 25 minutes from the cruise-terminal area to town. Allow 45 minutes initially and 45–75 minutes on final return for quay clearance, approved exit and the actual assigned berth. A town shuttle, when provided, is described as about 5 minutes; that is a ride time, not a published frequency or promise of free service. Obtain the day’s pickup position. Do not route a driver to the tourist marina or Le Havre cruise terminal.
